sector_level_search_notes: Ran 1 newsq per sector for all 11 sectors (3,5,6,8,9,12,14,16,17,22,23) plus 2 broader retries ('old Gurugram sectors property price per sq ft', 'metro old Gurugram prices soaring'). Every hit was a citywide or different-corridor story, not specific to sectors 3-23: (1) Moneycontrol 2026-04-17 'circle rates hiked by up to 75%' -- states collector rate rose from Rs 58,500 to Rs 84,825/sq yd (45%) but only for Sectors 63/63A/64/67 (SPR/Golf Course Ext corridor), not in our list. (2) HT 2026-08-07 (ANAROCK data) -- Gurugram citywide average residential price Rs 6,150/sq ft (2019) to Rs 13,350/sq ft (Q2 2026), +117%; citywide, not sector-specific. (3) BusinessToday 2025-07-24 advisor post -- concrete psf/per-sq-yd examples but all for Sectors 79, 93, 99-103 and 77 (SPR/UER-2/New Gurugram), none in our list. (4) Moneycontrol 2026-09-08 -- Dwarka Expressway corridor at Rs 21,700-24,000/sq ft, again a different corridor. (5) The Hindu 2026-08-10 -- Rs 271 Cr penthouse deal at DLF The Dahlias (Sector 63) at ~Rs 2.6 lakh/sq ft carpet, different sector. No article surfaced a price or appreciation figure tied to sectors 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16, 17, 22 or 23 specifically -- these are older/HUDA-era sectors and 2025-26 Gurugram real-estate press coverage is concentrated entirely on the newer growth corridors (SPR, Dwarka Expressway, Golf Course Extension Road, New Gurugram sectors 63-115+), so none were recorded per the 'skip an article that is really about a different sector' rule.
